questions.question: What is the probability that a leap year selected at random contains 53 Sundays?
questions.explanation: A leap year has 366 days = 52 weeks + 2 odd days. 52 weeks guarantee 52 Sundays. The 2 consecutive extra days can be: (Sun, Mon), (Mon, Tue), (Tue, Wed), (Wed, Thu), (Thu, Fri), (Fri, Sat), (Sat, Sun) -> 7 possible pairs. Sunday occurs in 2 pairs: (Sun, Mon) and (Sat, Sun). P(53 Sundays) = 2/7.

questions.question: A rectangular board measures 3 m by 2 m. A circular target of diameter 1 m lies entirely within the rectangle. A point is selected uniformly at random from the rectangle. What is the probability that the point lies inside the circular target?
questions.explanation: The point is uniformly distributed over the 3 m × 2 m rectangle, so probability is the target area divided by the rectangle area. The rectangle area is 3 × 2 = 6 m². The target radius is 0.5 m, so its area is π(0.5)² = π/4 m². Therefore P(inside target) = (π/4)/6 = π/24. This is a geometric-probability extension, not one of the specifically named core Class X outcomes in the 2026–27 CBSE syllabus.
